purpose: Hardens the WP 7.1+ client-side media processing integration by extracting placeholder data (dominant color/LQIP) server-side for new uploads and preventing the frontend from re-queueing missing conversions when client-side processing is active, plus HEIC/HEIF MIME mappings.
riskRationale: The new GD decode on every upload lacks the plugin's own dimension guard and runs even when placeholder data is never consumed, creating a memory-DoS/perf regression; additionally the placeholder path is only reachable when the conversion format is not 'none', so the headline fix may not run in the default configuration. No PII or auth issues found.

text: The re-queue guard and MIME mappings are correct and well-scoped, and the new placeholder helper reuses the existing deferred-commit pipeline cleanly. However, the new client-side placeholder path is gated behind the conversion hook (which is not registered when get_format() returns 'none' — the likely WP 7.1 case), and the helper decodes uploads unconditionally without the dimension guard that convert_image() applies, so it should not merge as-is.

reasoning: The fix works only in narrow configurations (format != 'none'), the new GD decode lacks the wppo_max_dimensions guard used elsewhere and runs even when placeholderType is the default 'svg', making the headline outcome unreliable and adding per-upload cost/risk. Fix reachability and gate/guard the decode before merge.

message: The re-queue guard is precisely scoped: it only suppresses add_img_into_queue() when client-side processing is active, while the file_exists() branches that serve already-converted images are untouched, so existing conversions are still served.

The new helper correctly reuses the existing extract_dominant_color()/generate_lqip()/store_placeholder_data() pipeline with the deferred-commit pattern, silently skips undecodable uploads, and frees the GD resource via imagedestroy(), mirroring existing code conventions.
heic/heif MIME mappings match the IANA-registered types (image/heic, image/heif) and are safe to emit in preload type attributes.

The client-side placeholder extraction is only reachable when the wp_generate_attachment_metadata filter is registered, and class-image-optimisation.php:138-143 skips registering it whenever get_format() returns 'none' (which is exactly what happens for the default 'webp'/'both' formats under WP 7.1+ because core_handles_next_gen() maps them to 'none'). In that primary scenario the new code never runs and new uploads still receive no placeholder data, contradicting the PR's stated outcome (Q1 Option B).
suggestion: Register the conversion/placeholder metadata filter independently of the next-gen format when client-side processing is enabled, so placeholder extraction runs even when get_format() is 'none'.

message: store_placeholder_data_for_upload() decodes the uploaded original with only the 20MB file-size guard. convert_image() (line 226-240) also enforces the wppo_max_dimensions filter (5000x5000) via getimagesize() BEFORE decoding to prevent decompression-bomb memory exhaustion. A small but highly-compressed PNG/WebP can decode into a multi-gigabyte bitmap and exhaust PHP's memory limit during the upload request, and under WP 7.1 the server-side sub-size generation that WordPress normally performs may be skipped, making this the first full decode of the file.
suggestion: Add the same getimagesize() + wppo_max_dimensions guard used in convert_image() before calling imagecreatefromstring().

message: store_placeholder_data_for_upload() runs unconditionally on every upload when client-side processing is enabled, even though the dominant_color/lqip data it produces is only consumed when placeholderType is 'dominant_color' or 'lqip'. The default placeholderType is 'svg' (class-main.php:204), so most sites pay a full file-read + GD decode of every uploaded image (up to 20MB) for data that is never used. On the server-side path this decode was a free byproduct of conversion; here it is entirely new work.
suggestion: Early-return from the client-side branch unless the configured placeholderType actually uses dominant-color/LQIP data.
